name: Continuous learning and adaptation
gist: Papers on how models can learn over time without forgetting old knowledge, and how to update models when the world changes without retraining from scratch.
explain: Retraining a large model from scratch takes weeks and costs thousands of dollars in computing. Yet the world changes — new data arrives, old patterns become irrelevant, and new patterns emerge. You need models that learn continuously, updating themselves as new information comes in, without forgetting everything they already know. This is the opposite of how most machine learning works today, where you train once on a big dataset and then deploy a static model.

The challenge is catastrophic forgetting: if you just train the old model on new data, it forgets the old patterns. Imagine teaching someone to play piano, then only training them on violin — they forget piano. You need to balance learning new things without erasing old knowledge. You also need to handle distribution shift, where the nature of the data changes over time (for example, if a model for medical diagnosis was trained on data from one hospital, it must adapt when it is deployed in a different hospital where patients and equipment are different). All of this must happen without constant retraining.

Researchers develop methods for continual learning. Some use memory buffers, keeping a small set of old examples so that when training on new data, the model still sees reminders of what it learned before. Some penalize large changes to the parameters that mattered for old tasks, making the model resist forgetting. Some use mixture-of-experts, where different specialized models handle different scenarios or time periods. Some design models that can quickly adapt to new domains with just a few examples, borrowing knowledge from similar domains they have seen before.

papers.title: Distributionally Robust Classification for Multi-source Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
papers.contribution: Provides efficient learning algorithm seamlessly integrated with existing UDA methods, consistently outperforming baselines especially when target data are extremely scarce.

papers.title: Forget Forgetting: Continual Learning in a World of Abundant Memory
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods while matching low computational cost of replay on class-incremental learning and continual instruction tuning.

papers.title: Spectral Collapse Drives Loss of Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Experiments on continual supervised and reinforcement learning tasks confirm that combining these two regularizers effectively preserves plasticity

papers.title: SplitLoRA: Balancing Stability and Plasticity in Continual Learning Through Gradient Space Splitting
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art continual learning performance through principled gradient space partitioning in LoRA-based framework.

papers.title: When and Where to Reset Matters for Long-Term Test-Time Adaptation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness across long-term TTA benchmarks with strong gains under challenging conditions through adaptive selective resets preserving beneficial knowledge.

papers.title: A Stronger Benchmark for Online Bilateral Trade: From Fixed Prices to Distributions
papers.contribution: Achieves Õ(T^3/4) regret under bounded-density conditions, closing separation between learning single prices versus distributions.

papers.title: AREA: Attribute Extraction and Aggregation for CLIP-Based Class-Incremental Learning
papers.contribution: Experiments show that AREA consistently outperforms SOTA methods.

papers.title: ICYM2I: The illusion of multimodal informativeness under missingness
papers.contribution: Framework addresses distribution shift from modality missingness, demonstrating importance of missingness adjustment on synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real-world datasets.

papers.title: IMSE: Intrinsic Mixture of Spectral Experts Fine-tuning for Test-Time Adaptation
papers.contribution: IMSE achieves state-of-the-art performance on single-domain TTA with 3.4pp improvement in CTTA using 2,000x fewer trainable parameters.

papers.title: KeepLoRA: Continual Learning with Residual Gradient Adaptation
papers.contribution: Balances all three objectives and achieves state-of-the-art continual learning performance for vision-language models.

papers.title: Memory-Free Continual Learning with Null Space Adaptation for Zero-Shot Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: NuSA-CL preserves zero-shot capabilities while achieving competitive continual learning performance with minimal memory and computational overhead.

papers.title: NEO — No-Optimization Test-Time Adaptation through Latent Re-Centering
papers.contribution: Improves ViT-Base ImageNet-C accuracy from 55.6% to 59.2% on single batch of 64 samples and beats all 7 baselines on multiple benchmarks with least compute.

papers.title: Prediction-Powered Risk Monitoring of Deployed Models for Detecting Harmful Distribution Shifts
papers.contribution: We demonstrate the effectiveness of PPRM through extensive experiments on image classification, large language model (LLM), and telecommunications monitoring tasks

papers.title: SCNS: Continual Personalization of Diffusion Models via Submodular Concept Neuron Selection
papers.contribution: Achieves fusion-free continual personalization by modifying only 0.41% of total parameters per concept while preventing catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: Source-Free Open-World RF Fingerprint Identification
papers.contribution: Achieves superior trade-off between old-class retention and new-class discovery, enabling secure access in dynamic wireless networks.

papers.title: StPR: Spatiotemporal Preservation and Routing for Exemplar-Free Video Class-Incremental Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves exemplar-free VCIL by preserving spatial semantics and temporal dynamics without requiring task IDs or stored exemplars.

papers.title: Test-time Domain Generalization for Image Super-resolution
papers.contribution: Effectively transfers feature distributions for SR networks with strong zero-shot generalization across diverse data distributions and network architectures.

papers.title: TokMem: Tokenized Procedural Memory for Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Outperforms retrieval-augmented generation on 1,000 tasks for atomic and compositional recall while avoiding repeated context overhead with far fewer parameters.

papers.title: Two-Way Is Better Than One: Bidirectional Alignment with Cycle Consistency for Exemplar-Free Class-Incremental Learning
papers.contribution: Analytically proves cycle loss contracts singular spectrum and achieves unprecedented reductions in catastrophic forgetting while maintaining high new-task accuracy.

papers.title: XIL: Cross-Expanding Incremental Learning
papers.contribution: XEED outperforms CIL baselines significantly on standard accuracy and novel BiDoT metrics for continual learning under domain-evolving conditions.
